2609.17331.title: Self-Emergence Agent Architecture:Behavior-Inertia HMM, Reflexive Metacognition,and Social-Contrastive Self-Modeling
2609.17331.paper_summary: Large language model (LLM) agents exhibit strong language-generation and problem-solving capabilities, yet suffer from three structural limitations: personality drift, non-evolutionary reflection, and the absence of a self-other boundary. Existing generative-agent simulations rely on static memory and fixed prompts, maintaining neither behavioral inertia nor endogenous self-evolution. We propose the Self-Emergence Agent Architecture (SEAA), which integrates three components: (i) a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) that encodes long-term behavioral and cognitive inertia as an editable state-transition matrix; (ii) a Reflexion-style verbal metacognition loop whose output updates the HMM parameters themselves, rather than merely being stored as text; and (iii) a multi-agent social environment in which initially identical agents continuously compare their behavior with others'. The three components form a closed loop: social action $\to$ feedback $\to$ self-reflection $\to$ inertia update $\to$ differentiated action. We state three falsifiable hypotheses and provide a reproducible experimental protocol with operational metrics. A language-model-free prototype shows the loop spontaneously breaks symmetry: initially identical agents consolidate distinct, stable personalities whereas matched controls do not. Experiments with a hosted LLM surface these differences as distinct first-person self-narratives, and a five-agent deliberation spontaneously develops social structure---a consensus hub and a unanimously rejected outlier---absent in the control. Following an epistemologically agnostic stance inspired by Zhuangzi, SEAA studies only observable behavioral emergence and makes no claim about subjective qualia. This work contributes a unified framework, a concrete architecture with pseudocode, mechanistic evidence, and a microscope-style sandbox for studying artificial-self emergence.
2609.17331.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）代理展現出強大的語言生成和問題解決能力，但卻存在三個結構性限制：個性漂移、非進化性反思，以及缺乏自我與他者的邊界。現有的生成代理模擬依賴靜態記憶和固定提示，既不維持行為慣性，也不具內生自我進化。我們提出了自我出現代理架構（SEAA），它整合了三個組件：（i）一個隱馬可夫模型（HMM），將長期行為和認知慣性編碼為可編輯的狀態轉移矩陣；（ii）一個反思風格的語言元認知循環，其輸出更新HMM參數本身，而不僅僅是作為文本存儲；以及（iii）一個多代理社會環境，其中最初相同的代理不斷與他者比較其行為。這三個組件形成一個閉環：社會行動 $\to$ 反饋 $\to$ 自我反思 $\to$ 慣性更新 $\to$ 差異化行動。我們陳述了三個可證偽的假設，並提供了一個可重複的實驗協議及操作性指標。一個不依賴語言模型的原型顯示該循環自發打破對稱：最初相同的代理鞏固出不同且穩定的個性，而匹配的對照組則沒有。與託管的LLM進行的實驗顯示這些差異作為不同的第一人稱自我敘事，而五個代理的討論自發發展出社會結構——一個共識中心和一個一致被拒絕的異類——在對照組中不存在。遵循受到莊子啟發的認識論上不可知的立場，SEAA僅研究可觀察的行為出現，並不對主觀質感提出任何主張。本研究貢獻了一個統一框架、一個具體的架構與偽代碼、機械證據，以及一個顯微鏡式的沙盒，用於研究人工自我出現。
2609.17331.author: Xiaoyang Liu et.al.
